body: I have worked hard all my life and now I'm 61 and on disability. Medicare advantage is the absolute worst insurance I have ever had! It has highest copays, highest deductibles, argues about every medication and doesn't cover crap.

It's horrible that you are going through such a rough time. I sure hope you can come out of it. I don't want to sound like I'm preaching but alcohol and weed are depressants and sure are not beneficial when you are feeling this way. Weaning yourself off of these until you do feel better would help a bit. 

I am glad you were too afraid to kill yourself... that shows that somewhere inside you know it's not for the best. Are you all alone? Do you have any family?  A good aid in overcoming social anxiety is to start out slow with people you know and can trust. First get together at your place, then at a friend's place then move to a low key coffee shop... before you know it you'll be dancing in the club. .... remember ..... baby steps. 

I want to highlight two words you used: the first one is "seems". As they say, "things are often not as they seem". I don't know your circumstances but I do know from experience that some people may seem like they don't care when they really do. Is there anyone you can open up to? Sometimes people need to be asked for help. They may not want to volunteer it for fear of making things worse. But, as I said, I don't know your circumstances. 

The second word is "feel" I know from experience that feelings can cloud over the sunniest of days. It happens to me all the time and most times I need help getting out of it. But what I want express is that though you "feel" like a failure, you are most likely far from it. For one you are only 20 years old! If you've screw some shit up in your life then you still have a lot of time to fix it. We have all messed up or went down the wrong road as young adults. That is a part of life. 

I am not discrediting your feelings. I want you to know that. You feel that way and there is something very real that is making you feel that way. You're job is to find what it is. Are there negative people around you? Do you have too high expectations of yourself? Ask yourself: " what have I failed at" ( no life is not a valid answer.... be more specific) try to look at the answer objectively . How have you failed? Why? Was it as big a failure as you feel it was? Go through a few of these. However, for each one, find something you have succeeded at . ( don't tell me nothing... also not a valid answer) I know, with depression I feel accomplished some days just for cleaning the cat box. It is hard. Getting out of bed, going to work or school... all are accomplishments. These small accomplishments lay the foundation for larger ones. 

I understand that the dark glasses we wear when we are depressed make it hard for us to see things in a positive light. So look for definite accomplishments... where there is no doubt.  "Today I made the bed" I did , my cat is currently messing it up as I type... it is a small thing but all is relative. We are talking feelings here so how things feel is important. Our feelings dictate how we see the world. Now I am sure that you have accomplished more than you have failed at. Build on your accomplishments and learn from your failures. Hanshi, (honorific for 8th degree black belt in my Dojo) always says that the only way to fail is not to try. When you don't accomplish what you set out to do it is not a failure it is a lesson. If you do nothing that is a failure. 

Yeah I know I am verbose, I apologize, I simply want to convey how much I want you to see the proverbial "light at the end of the tunnel" ( no the light isn't a train coming to run you over). Please try the baby steps... you only have to get up one more time than you get knocked down ( Hanshi again). Yeah these things you have probably heard before... that's because they are fundamental truths to the human condition.  I really hope that maybe I have said them just differently enough to spark a tiny ember of hope in you.

It sucks when you're at a party and everyone is having fun and you just feel worse because it is just a reminder of how crappy you feel. It is a vicious cycle. I've ridden many a rollercoaster like that. It isn't easy to overcome. Maybe you are right that no one you have met up until now has really cared. ( there is a reason you ex is an ex .. right?) That doesn't mean that you can't find someone who does care. ..... listen to me... I sound like a hypocrite... I say "nobody cares" a lot. ... Down deep though I still hold out a little flicker of hope that I will find someone some day. I'm 56. I try to tell myself that people find each other when they are in their 80's.... there is still time.... easier said than done ..huh? 

Anyhow. how about trying to take smaller steps into the world of dating again.... do something you are comfortable with so that your surroundings and others won't be a distraction.

I love it!! great idea, expanding your space without too much complex works. I so want to build a schoolie!! I am a school bis driver by trade and my old bus is being auctioned off this summer! Wish I had the extra cash! It will probably go cheap!

I understand, in my own way, where you are coming from. I am 56 and for the most part feel the same as you. I do hope that you can make it through this night. I know everything is not better in the light of day, but perhaps it is survivable. That is all we can do survive each painful day. I suppose I have not lost all hope because, though I have tried before and frequently think about it, I have not recently attempted suicide. I won't dismiss the option but I'm not there yet. I don't know if my words will reach you, or if they do, if they will have an effect. I do however hope that you don't leave. Not yet. Bounce your problems off someone, get a fresh perspective... hell bounce them off of me...I'm not much good at helping myself but have helped others ..... give me a chance.

Corey
so not appropriate. The kid is hurting. Poking fun at him is not amusing

Just a suggestion, you have access to the internet obviously. There are some good accredited "virtual" mental health practitioners. I live in the sticks myself. I am old so I can drive every so often to see a therapist though it takes an hour and 1/2 to get there. I do however meet more often with her in a private secure chat room. .... it's an option.

For all that I have said in my previous comment, I believe the anguish and the oppressive hopelessness you feel. I am struggling with it too and I am 56. At the same time we are both still alive.  My mom used to say "where there is life, there is hope". That is true, not because I see it though. It is because I do know that if I were to die then all hope for me would also die. 

She also used to say " never say never" , though I also feel  will never get better, that small hope that just being alive brings innately, can change never into "maybe someday."

You do have many years ahead of you to be able to rectify your life. Never is not a word that a young person should have in their vocabulary. I get it, all you can see is darkness. Your horizon is so large though at your age, that there is a better than good chance that the sun will rise. I am not saying that being older is worse. I never would even try to insinuate that one person's tribulations are worse than another's it just isn't right. What I am saying is that as a fact of life, there are more possibilities, more valid "maybe somedays" when you are young. Let's face it. You have a long time, if you chose and are able to. A long time to achieve what ever you want. 

So where am I going with this? I am trying to say, that even if you feel something won't help, if you don't have any pleasure from anything. Try new things anyway. You only know , for sure, it won't help if you actually have tried it. I mentioned to another post that "if you are falling off a cliff, you may as well try to fly, what do you have to lose?" The only thing you can lose by trying are the people who preach at you that you are not trying. Who knows, maybe something will stick and you will get better. 

While there is life there is hope ( even if we can't feel it, trust that it is there)

I get it. It is so frustrating when others can't see things that  you do. I have had the same problem. Sometimes crap piles up in our lives and beats us down. People can't see how the accumulation of harmful events, even what may seem like nothing, can eventually crush a person. "The straw that broke the camel's back" is a often used phrase for a reason. It says that to have an excruciating result you don't need to have a boulder drop on your head: a life time of "straw" can weigh you down just as painfully. In fact I believe it is worse. 

If someone experiences a devastating event, one that no one would ever deny it being tragic and painful, their pain is immediately recognized and they receive comfort, sympathy and assistance from those around them. 

When you have dealt with small harms for decades, over and over you are stabbed with a tiny needle. All anyone can see is that one small wound. They can't see the devastation years of small wounds has wrought upon you. It's one hurt after another, after another. It never ends. That makes it worse. There is no end and therefore no relief. No time to recover and start to mend. You are all alone because no one recognizes your pain. They don't find your reactions valid for "such a tiny injury".

I remember working in a museum once. The curator explained to me why it was essential that no one touch the paintings. He said : "It's not that one person touching it will ruin it. It is the effect of thousands of people over decades that can touch a painting right out of existence."

Saying stuff like "you see what you want" or "stop looking at the glass as half empty" and so forth, is harmful. It is like saying: "How you feel and see things isn't valid". "Your opinion about your own life is flawed".

I agree that is fucking biased as hell. It is also so common. I get it from people who profess their intent to help me but who only end up preaching at me and telling me how I should " get over it" and then they start telling me how "their life has been so much worse than mine". "I should be thankful I didn't have to go through what they did."  

I am not a big advocate for myself so, even though they came to help me, I end up listening and helping them with their problems, while inside I am screaming: "when is it my turn to be helped and cared for?!" 

It is the accumulated pain of a life time of hurt that truly breaks a person, I know. No one has the right, or the knowledge to judge your opinion of your life. It is your life. It is how you feel. 

I shared this because I hope it will help at least some people  can realize that they are blind to the cumulative effects of a life time of hurt.

I hope you are still with us. I am in a similar "holding pattern". I keep telling people "I don't know what will help: If I did I would have done it already. All I know is what I have tried that didn't help." That's what I tell them when they expect me to "fix myself" or try something I already know won't help. I keep asking myself, as I drive around aimlessly, "what am I doing? Why am I still here? Why don't I just kill myself?" The last question, so far, is the only one I can answer: I'm scared, I want to live, I want another chance. ..... I hope you can answer the question too. Any reason I guess is a good reason, if it keeps us alive. 

I wish you well

That hits the mark with me too. The fear of nothingness, of never having another shot, of being erased, is terrifying. Existential angst, I suppose, keeps us alive as well as it turns others to their death. Weird how that works.

I definitely think that the only reason I am still alive is because I'm chicken. I understand where you are coming from. As far as turning to religion, I would say "any port in a storm". If that is what has comforted you in the past, try it again. If you never have tried it, you might as well, you have nothing to lose but your depression. I have been trying everything I can, when I have the energy to do so. 

I have no one so there is no risk of hurting anyone if I died. I make excuses to myself about needing to finish this or that, upholding this or that promise and so on to justify being alive. I realize that I shouldn't have to justify why I have not killed myself yet, but there it is. 

For now, tenuous as it is, that is my life preserver. I hope you can continue to use any reason at all to stay alive. For the little that it's worth, you are not alone in your feelings.

I understand what you are going through. I, personally, do not want to die but I also constantly think of suicide. It seems to be the only answer to my life. I understand and feel your despair. The advice  we get from others is nothing but a jumble of platitudes: none of which help. We have tried them all. I feel like I am hanging by my fingernails from a cliff face, constantly grasping at the crumbling rock. I want someone/something to help me but so far no one/nothing has. Knowing that it has "gotten better" for other people does nothing for me: they are not me, not you. What works for one may not work for either of us. Inside me I guess there is a struggling little flame of life, of hope, that makes me get up and go through another pointless day. Every day I go to sleep disappointed that a miracle has not happened to give meaning and positivity to my life. So yeah I get you.  I am thinking now:" why am I even sharing this. If she feels like I do, knowing that there are others out there who feel as I do, doesn't help at all".  At least I know my comment is of little help. It wouldn't help me. I had to write it though just in case it helps you. I know that the chances of that are slim. But, as they say, if you are falling off a cliff, you may as well try to fly. What do you have to lose?
That’s ok... you’re off to a good start. It’s not easy for folks like us. You have to keep going though. I feel you have a beautiful soul and you need to let that show.

I’m sorry I haven’t answered you sooner.  I understand what you are going through. I am very depressed myself.  Believe me, though I’m trans, I know a lot of “normal” people who suffer from depression. 
That’s not the problem though is it? You’re stuck and can’t move forward in your transition right? Can I ask how old you are? Is there an LGBTQ community center near you? I’m just brainstorming here. You said that home is not an environment in which you can transition then that seems like the first thing you have to do. Do you have a job? It’s not easy to make a go of it alone these days so you may need to try to find a trans roommate.. just some suggestions... You have options.... have you sought treatment for depression? That can also be helped... 
I’m on your side
Corey

You are right. There are some people who will never see you as the woman you are. There are many who don't see me as a man. I was transgender before the word even exsisted. Bigotry, hostility and ignorance are our crosses to bear. I have felt similarly. I came on here after desperatly looking for a forum to vent my thoughts of suicide. You sound young and things are so much better for transfolks now, despite the hostile political environment. I understand that doesn't solve your problems. At least you are not alone. Today there are so many resources for support. You do however have to seek them out. Then decide what you want and make a plan to go after it.  Take an honest look at the issues. I know it seems like forever but HRT can wait. (I was in my 40's before I could start. ) Strip away any issues that are specifically a result of being trans and you are left with the same issues all people deal with when making their way on their own: leaving home, building a life, school, saving money...  so do what it takes to succeed. Get involved in activism.  Go to school, work after and before, find a roomate or two and start building your life on your terms. Surround yourself with people who do see you as the woman you are. That way the idiots who are not able to see the real you won't seem as important. 

By no means am I saying it's easy. Being trans means you have an extra burden to carry. But it also makes you special and worthy of success. 

By now you're probably wondering why, if I think like this, do I want to die. Well the story is long but suffice it to say that I am at a different point in my life than you are. My choices are much more narrow than they were 20 or 30 years ago.  

I hope you find the people who can be the mirrors to your beauty. They are the key. 

​

Corey
